title: Building a Tiny Standardized Interpretability-to-Safety Benchmark

original_idea.body:
# Building a Tiny Standardized Interpretability-to-Safety Benchmark

**Problem:** There are no widely adopted interpretability benchmarks; a key open problem is whether mechanistic findings translate to safety guarantees.

**Direction:** Design a minimal benchmark (fixed safety concepts, fixed open model, scoring protocol for detection AUROC, causal specificity, robustness) and release with baselines.

**Why it matters:** A shared yardstick is missing infrastructure flagged by Open Phil. Self-contained deliverable.

**Relevant context:** Open Phil RFP; SAELens/Neuronpedia.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (shared benchmark advances interp-to-safety) but standardization-to-catastrophe link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Assemble a small benchmark + baselines from public SAEs/models; guided, design effort.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Self-contained benchmark + baselines deliverable, though benchmark design has breadth.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Inherently lab-independent infrastructure flagged as a priority; public material.

low_compute.reasoning: Baseline runs on public SAEs/models; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Interp benchmarks are an acknowledged gap; a small standardized one may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Interp-to-safety benchmark is a known gap; a concrete small prototype may be open.
